title: See What a Living-stone
description: See What a Living-stone in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 118, part 5, headed “An hosanna for the Lord's day; or, A new song of salvation by Christ”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: See what a liv-ing stone The buil-ders did re-fuse; Yet God hath built his church there-on In spite of en-vious Jews.

lines: Yet God hath built his church thereon
Yet on this rock shall Zion rest,
The work, O Lord, is thine,
This day declares it all divine,
Let us rejoice, and sing, and pray,
Let all the church be glad.
Bless him, ye saints; he comes to bring
And offer on thine altar, Lord,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
